title: Selenium protects neonates against neurotoxicity from prenatal exposure to manganese.
ehr_evidence: Data were collected prospectively through face-to-face interviews, umbilical cord blood sampling, and clinical NBNA tests.
summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating the protective effect of prenatal selenium against manganese-induced neurotoxicity in neonates using cord blood metal levels and behavioral assessments.
key_findings: High cord blood Mn (≥P75, ≥9.1 μg/L) was associated with lower NBNA scores (adjusted ß = -1.2, 95% CI: -1.4 to -1.0, p<0.001) and higher risk of low NBNA (adjusted OR = 8.0, 95% CI: 2.8 to 23.0, p<0.001).

With low cord Se (<P50, <63.1 μg/L), Mn was negatively associated with NBNA scores (adjusted ß = -1.1, 95% CI: -1.3 to -0.9, p<0.001) and increased risk of low NBNA (adjusted OR = 5.7, 95% CI: 2.8 to 11.5, p<0.001).
With high cord Se (≥P50, ≥63.1 μg/L), the adverse effect of Mn was attenuated (NBNA: adjusted ß = 0.1, 95% CI: -0.3 to 0.5, p = 0.746; Low NBNA: adjusted OR = 4.5, 95% CI: 0.4 to 46.7, p = 0.205).
High Mn/low Se group had significantly lower NBNA scores than high Mn/high Se group (38.0 ± 1.6 vs 39.5 ± 0.9, p<0.001).
Mn/Se ratio was moderately correlated with NBNA scores (r = -0.41, p<0.001).
data_source_type: primary prospective cohort (interviews, biospecimens, clinical exams)
population: 933 term newborns and mothers in Shanghai, China (2008-2009)
limitations: dietary manganese and selenium intake not assessed
potential residual confounding despite multivariable adjustment
